input: A centrifugal pump plays a crucial role in transferring caustic solution between two vessels that are located at grade, and its performance at the selected duty point is summarised here. At this duty point, the pump delivers a flow of 24 m3 h-1 against a head of 64 m, operating at an efficiency of 81%, which together result in a shaft power requirement of 5.2 kW. In other words, the motor driving the pump must be capable of supplying this power at the shaft in order to sustain the required flow against the system head. To provide a comfortable margin, the motor is rated 15% above this value, ensuring that the drive is not operating at the very edge of its capability. Furthermore, cavitation is often a major concern in pumping applications, and it is therefore reassuring to note that no cavitation was observed during the acceptance test. It should be emphasised, however, that this test was conducted over a period of 4 h and covered the duty point only, meaning that behaviour at other operating points, such as higher flows or reduced suction heads, remains untested. Overall, these figures provide a clear and concise snapshot of the duty that the pump was selected to perform, highlighting the interplay between flow, head, efficiency, and power in a single operating point. Taken as a whole, the duty point therefore encapsulates the essential bargain of the selection: a specified flow, delivered against a specified head, at a stated efficiency and a corresponding shaft power, with a sensibly margined motor and an acceptance test that, while reassuring in its own terms, was confined to that single point on the characteristic curve.
target: A centrifugal pump moves caustic solution between two vessels at grade. At the duty point, the flow is 24 m3 h-1 against a head of 64 m, and the pump efficiency is 81%. Shaft power at the duty point is 5.2 kW. The duty point is the operating point the pump was selected for. The head is the lift the system imposes at that flow, read from the system curve where it crosses the pump curve, and the shaft power is the power the motor must deliver to the pump shaft to hold the point. Efficiency relates the shaft power to the hydraulic power imparted to the liquid; the balance of the shaft power leaves the pump as heat in the casing and the liquid. The motor is rated 15% above the duty shaft power, so the drive holds the duty point below its rating. Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test, which ran for 4 h at the duty point only. The observation covers the duty point. Operation away from the duty point, at higher flow or at lower suction head, sits outside the tested condition, and cavitation there is neither confirmed nor excluded by the test. The duty figures describe one point on the pump's range; behaviour across the range, and the margin between the duty point and the ends of the curve, are separate matters from the duty-point selection itself. Caustic service adds a materials condition to the duty: the casing, the impeller, and the seal faces are chosen for the liquid, and their suitability is part of the selection that the duty point summarises, although it is not stated in the duty figures themselves.
